term: bodily nature as cognitive object rather than constitution
definition: A nature n occurring in CanUnderstand intellect n is an object of the represented capacity, not thereby a constitutive bodily nature of the intellectual principle. This interface distinction does not assert a modern material theory of representation, nor does it supply an account of intentionality.
note: Needed to prevent a content/constitution equivocation. The source q.75 a.1 ad 2 distinguishes a likeness received potentially from what is naturally actual in a knower; that context motivates keeping the relations separate without formalizing the complete reception account.
